title: Quantum tests via inequalities for joint statistics
abstract: In this work we derive statistical inequalities whose violation is equivalent to the impossibility of describing the data by a genuine joint probability distribution. So they are witnesses of the failure of a common probability space. We examine whether the most significant quantum quasidistributions violate these inequalities. We examine also whether these inequalitites are violated by the joint distributions derived form a noisy joint measurement. As a relevant example we find violations for the maximally mixed state, as well as cases where all system states violate them. This points to the idea that these results are more than a property of the system states, but are instead a property of the statistical structure of quantum mechanics.
summary: This paper develops and tests a family of statistical inequalities designed to detect when data cannot be explained by a standard joint probability distribution. By analyzing violations using various quasi-probability representations (like Wigner and P functions) and modeling noisy measurements, the authors argue that these violations reveal fundamental structural properties of quantum mechanics itself.
main_problem: The work derives statistical inequalities whose violation proves that observed data cannot be described by a genuine joint probability distribution, acting as witnesses to the failure of a common probability space.
main_result: Violation of these inequalities is found for the maximally mixed state and generally suggests that the non-classicality detected is a property of the quantum statistical structure itself, rather than solely the system state.
method: The authors derive specific mathematical inequalities relating joint probabilities (e.g., $p_{AB} \leq p_{AC} + p_{BC}$) and test them using various quasi-probability distributions (Wigner, P, Q) and noisy measurement models.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on observables acting on a qubit (two-dimensional Hilbert space), characterized by dichotomic measurements ($\pm 1$). The study compares results across different mathematical representations of quantum states and correlations.
key_observables: Joint probabilities $p_{XY}(x, y)$, the correlation factor $\eta$, and the quantity $S^2$ derived from expectation values of combinations of observables.
important_parameters: The state purity parameter ($\mu$), noise factors ($\gamma$), and the structure constants defining the measurement operators ($s_A, s_B, s_C$).
main_assumptions: Assumptions are made when constructing quasi-probability distributions (like Wigner or P functions) to ensure structural properties like positivity or correct marginals. The analysis also models noisy measurements using noise factors $\gamma$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the fundamental statistical inequality, to testing it against various quasi-distributions (Wigner, P, Q), and finally developing a practical framework for analyzing violations under realistic noisy measurement conditions.
why_interesting: This work delves into the foundational mathematical structure of quantum correlations by establishing necessary conditions (inequalities) that any classical joint probability distribution must satisfy. Violations point to non-classicality rooted in the statistical formalism, which is crucial for understanding fundamental limits in quantum measurements and information processing.
